paper_metadata.title: Quantum-enhanced versus classical Support Vector Machine: An application to stock index forecasting

summary: The paper reports two NISQ quantum-kernel SVM experiments on IBM Quantum Experience: a 3-qubit TSX forecasting task using lagged TSX/SPX/CAD returns, and a 2-qubit SX5E forecasting task using same-date DAX/CAC returns. In both cases the quantum-enhanced SVM is outperformed by the classical SVM, with the paper stating the quantum runtime averages 3 hours 55 minutes per observation and is about 5.9×10^6 times slower than local classical computation.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced SVM (quantum kernel estimator) versus classical SVM for forecasting the future weekly movement direction of the S&P/TSX composite index using lagged TSX, SPX, and CAD returns.

algorithm.variant: quantum-enhanced SVM using quantum kernel estimator (SVM-QKE / QSVM)

hyperparameters.C: tested over multiple values (exact values not reported)
hyperparameters.gamma: not used for quantum kernel; classical RBF kernel gamma tuned (exact values not reported)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 features mapped to 3 qubits for the TSX experiment; classical returns are embedded into a second-order Pauli-Z evolution feature map
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of next-week TSX direction: Direction_TSX(t+1) = f(Return_TSX(t), Return_SPX(t), Return_CAD(t))

problem_instance.description: Weekly binary classification of future TSX index movement direction using lagged returns of TSX, SPX, and CAD

dataset_specification.preprocessing: weekly Wednesday sampling; use one-week lag returns; binary up/down labels; rolling monthly evaluation
dataset_specification.train_test_split: 80 consecutive weeks training, 20 consecutive weeks testing; repeated monthly over 113 Wednesdays

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use Wednesday observations to avoid end-of-week volatility; construct lagged returns; binary labels for up/down movement; limited sample due to 5-qubit cloud access
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 113 repeated rolling evaluations; metrics summarized as means across runs; balanced accuracy, F1-score, precision, recall

noise_model.noise_type: NISQ / hardware noise not further specified

implementation_details.framework_version: Qiskit 0.19.6 documentation referenced; exact runtime version not reported
implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn SVC for classical baseline; classical SVM dual solved classically for QKE
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Standard SVM preprocessing on financial returns; rolling-window training/testing
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical SVM decision rule and metric aggregation over 113 runs
implementation_details.total_execution_time: average 3 hours 55 minutes per observation on quantum device; classical local computation much faster
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: average 3 hours 55 minutes per observation (includes queue/waiting and execution as reported)

results.unit: times slower than classical local computation

speedup_claims.conditions: cited from prior literature; assumes quantum access to data in coherent superposition
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states this is a theoretical claim from the literature, not an empirical speedup in this experiment.

speedup_claims.conditions: average per observation on IBM Quantum Experience / Qiskit cloud device
speedup_claims.caveats: Includes queue/waiting and execution; runtime varied from 40 minutes to more than 8 hours.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log N) for quantum SVM kernel-based classification (theoretical claim cited from literature)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for classical SVM (as stated in paper)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: ~3h55m per observation on cloud quantum device
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: local classical computation; average 5.9×10^6 times faster than quantum

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper reports only 113 rolling evaluations on a 3-qubit quantum kernel model with 80/20 train/test windows
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Substantially larger, lower-noise fault-tolerant hardware and much faster kernel evaluation; current setup is a 3-qubit NISQ experiment
limiting_factors: Classical SVM outperforms the quantum-enhanced SVM on the reported metrics
Quantum runtime is extremely slow relative to classical
Only 3 qubits and small rolling windows are used
NISQ noise and limited qubit availability
Theoretical O(log N) speedup is not realized in practice

notes: Hardware is IBM Quantum Experience / Qiskit on an actual quantum computer, described as a freely publicly available cloud-based quantum device; specific backend name not given.
The paper states the TSX feature map uses nqb = 3 qubits and two repetitions with full entanglement.
The paper cites theoretical SVM complexity O(N) classical and O(log N) quantum from prior literature; this is not an empirical benchmark claim.
Paper explicitly states the quantum-enhanced SVM does not demonstrate better performance in accuracy or computation time than the classical SVM.
